summary:
ECHOES: The Forgotten Voices of Space is an interactive web museum about eight robotic explorers that no longer transmit, including Opportunity, Spirit, Viking 1 and Ingenuity.

Each explorer has a 3D robot that acts out its story in five emotional chapters, a mission file with key dates, findings and source links, and a console where visitors question an AI reconstruction grounded in the mission record. A Kids' Space retells three NASA missions with simple stories and a star quiz.

This is our answer to "Abandoned but Not Forgotten". Archives keep these machines' data, but data alone does not make young people care. ECHOES pairs emotion with accuracy: every voice is labelled as an educational reconstruction, and facts link to their sources.

These machines changed what we know about other worlds. The next generation should know their stories.
details:
What it does and how it works

ECHOES is a web museum of eight robotic explorers that no longer transmit. A visitor arrives through a short opening film, then sees a "ledger of signals": a timeline showing how long each mission spoke to Earth, its planned lifetime, and the silence since. Choosing an explorer opens three things: a 3D robot that acts out its story in five chapters (arrival, discovery, trouble, silence, echo), a mission file with key dates, findings, a myth check and source links, and a console where the visitor can ask questions to an AI reconstruction of the explorer. A separate Kids' Space retells three NASA missions with simple stories, a 3D robot children can play with, and a star quiz.

Benefits and intended impact

ECHOES turns archive records into stories that teenagers and children can feel and remember. We want visitors to leave knowing what these machines discovered, how each one fell silent, and why it still matters, and to become curious about space exploration.

Tools and technology

The site is a single web page written in HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The 3D robots, terrain and lighting are generated in code with the three.js library. The timeline is drawn in SVG and the signal traces on canvas. We used Claude as our AI assistant to build the site and write its texts, and it also powers the live conversations and the read-aloud voice. The opening film was generated with Gemini and is labelled on screen as an AI illustration. No special hardware is needed: the site runs in a web browser.

How it is creative

Instead of describing the explorers, we let them speak. Each robot shows emotion through movement and light: it looks around in wonder, hops with joy at a discovery, trembles in a dust storm, lowers its head when the signal ends, and lifts it again as an "echo".

What we considered

Accuracy came first. Every voice is labelled as an educational reconstruction, never a real transmission. The AI answers only from a mission fact sheet and is told not to invent dates or quotes. Facts link to their sources. We also designed for two audiences, teenagers
